notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, census arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + concept-census evidence (which concepts and domains selected the pole)); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Strongest hits are verbs/nouns that introduce a demonstration or depiction (illustrate, demonstrate, show, 'image/snapshot/visualization of') in scientific or reporting prose, plus scattered weak commas and 'of' in similar slots; the census hit on diseases in neutral frames does not obviously fit, so this is a best guess with mixed coverage. Near misses keep topic and syntax but replace the showing word with an unrelated action.
